name: Who starts late
finding: NIST's causal model runs cues to milling to pre-evacuation actions to delay, so the dispositions that drive milling should decide who is early and who is late.
notes: The weights and the ordering are ours; the magnitudes are the paper's. Which published fit applies is a property of the BUILDING, selected by the scenario's alarm quality - Proulx's 515 s is a building mean that already includes the residents who could not hear it, so moving an individual to the poor-alarm fit would count audibility twice. Within that fit, not hearing the alarm is the single heaviest term, which is where audibility belongs. Three things this deliberately does not do: add gathering seconds on top (the fit already covers actions before leaving, so a commitment pushes a resident later in the same queue instead), scale for being asleep (the scenario's day/night fit carries that), or scale for anything at all (a scale on a quantile moves the realized mean off the published one).

name: Asleep or deaf to the alarm
finding: Waking is part of pre-movement, and the night fit already reflects a sleeping population.
notes: PARKED AND OFF, and kept to record why. Both of the obvious scalings here would double-count: being asleep is already in which distribution the scenario selects, and not hearing the alarm is handled by stratifying the ranking instead. A scale on a quantile also breaks the thing the quantile mechanism is for - it moves the realized mean off the published one.

name: How fast they walk
finding: The registry already draws a speed per resident from the measured mean and spread.
notes: Carried straight across: the registry's own speed heuristics did this work already, so compiling it is a unit-for-unit copy.

name: Who gives up on a queue first
finding: Nobody has measured who waits and who reroutes. Risk tolerance standing in for it is a guess.
notes: Both the ordering and the distribution are unmeasured here, so this is the weakest chain in the model and a prime candidate for the sensitivity run.

name: Who presses on into smoke
finding: The share who turn back at each visibility is measured; which individuals they are is not.
notes: The distribution is SOURCED and the ordering is ESTIMATE, so the chain is ESTIMATE. The compiler reports the weaker of the two rather than the flattering one.

name: Who tries the other staircase
finding: About a quarter try the other staircase; the ones who know the building are likelier to be among them.

name: You cannot try a staircase you do not know about
finding: Residents chose familiar stairs over nearer ones, and cannot choose one they have never noticed.
notes: A gate rather than a weight: this is not a tendency, it is an impossibility. Runs last so it overrides whatever the quantile assigned.

name: Stairs available at all
finding: Whether a resident can use stairs is a fact about them rather than a draw.

name: Time spent gathering
finding: Summed over whatever this resident will not leave without.
notes: Reported for engines that model gathering as its own state. Engines whose pre-movement fit already includes pre-evacuation actions should ignore it, and the adapter decides which - see adapters/*.toml.

name: Not knowing the building
finding: Residents chose familiar stairs over nearer ones, so unfamiliarity should cost something on route choice.
notes: No reference distribution, so this currently produces nothing: the Outputs tab leaves route_confusion without one because no published figure was found. It is here to be visible as a gap rather than forgotten.

name: Habitual staircase
finding: Residents chose familiar stairs over the nearest ones.

name: Neighbours they would warn
finding: 30 to 34 percent of WTC occupants helped others, and this is how many they could reach.
notes: Counts every tie, which overstates it: a building-chat tie is not a knock on the door. Narrowing it needs the tie kinds, which the compiler cannot currently see.
